_comment: Source of truth for home.microprediction.org. Organized by research theme so related work sits together; within each theme list published work first, then preprints/working drafts. Edit this, then run build.py. Run scan.py to discover newer drafts across the package repos. Each paper: 'venue' (presence implies published — rendered in italics), 'links' [{label,url}], optional 'draft_new' to mark a link labelled 'latest draft'.

highlight.body:
Scaling econometrics to millions of variables in this paper (site: winning.microprediction.org).

Second place: the unification of the two sides of portfolio theory, in this paper (site: schur.microprediction.org).

Third place: a very hard to beat autonomous univariate distributional forecaster, in this paper (site: skaters.microprediction.org).

Fourth place: generalizing every closed-form quant model to regime switching, in regimelib (sites: regimeswitching.org and homogenization.microprediction.org).

ultra.description: Twelve current papers worth your time, ranked for useful ideas and demonstrated value. Close companions share a slot; adjacent ranks are approximate.

entries.title: Scalable Inversion of Contests with Correlated Performances, Including Softmax and Multinomial Probit
entries.why: Correlated probit inversion at a million alternatives. Makes a richer choice model computationally usable; the engine behind much of the contest programme.
entries.caveat: Linear scaling assumes fixed structural complexity and numerical resolution.
entries.heritage: The 2021 horse-race inversion; conditional independence and quadrature.

entries.title: Schur Complementary Allocation: A Unification of Hierarchical Risk Parity and Minimum Variance Portfolios
entries.why: HRP and minimum variance become two ends of one dial. The organising result behind the Schur programme; read the interior-optimum companion next.
entries.caveat: Portfolio gains still depend on covariance estimation, constraints and damping choice.

entries.title: Transforms All the Way Down: Automatic Online Distributional Forecasting by Conjugation
entries.why: A full distributional forecaster built from reversible transforms. Working software and a strong FRED showing make it a baseline expensive models should have to beat.
entries.caveat: GARCH-t wins the asset-price comparison; density reconstruction can change benchmark verdicts.
entries.heritage: PITs, change of variables and online residual forecasting.

entries.title: Scoring Point-Cloud Distributional Submissions: The Nearest-the-Pin Parimutuel, Jittered Outcomes, and the Heat Ladder
entries.why: KDE scoring can reward an artificially sharpened cloud. Diagnoses the distortion, repairs population incentives and turns smoothing scales into separate rewards.
entries.caveat: Fixed bandwidths; finite clouds and proportional pot payouts need separate treatment.
entries.heritage: Bröcker–Smith, Ferro and relative de Bruijn.

entries.title: On a Simple Relationship Between Order Imbalance, Skew and Width in Over-the-Counter Trading
entries.why: Imbalanced OTC quoting becomes a balanced problem by shifting skew and rescaling carrying cost. An exact symmetry that saves a fresh optimization.
entries.caveat: Interior steady-state exponential quotes only; quote-floor clipping can break it.
entries.heritage: The auction model of Trading Illiquid Goods.

entries.title: Security and Derivative Pricing with Fast Regime Switches
entries.why: One small linear system prices a broad family of switching models. A reusable engine, with fast-switching corrections and numerical fallbacks.
entries.caveat: Noncommuting parameter switches need other routes; the expansion is not always fastest.
entries.heritage: Cotton’s thesis, singular perturbation and Markov-chain group inverses.

entries.title: Structured Gaussian Argmax Layers
entries.why: The contest engine becomes a differentiable Gaussian choice layer: winner probabilities, potential and gradients from one shared calculation. One of the highest ceilings on this list.
entries.caveat: Low rank helps; faster neural training remains an open bet.
entries.heritage: Random utility, perturbed optimizers and Fenchel–Young losses.

entries.title: HumpDay: Derivative-Free Optimizers in Pure Python and JavaScript, with a Contamination-Resistant Real-World Benchmark
entries.why: Optimizer recommendations you can interrogate: portable implementations, hard budgets and objectives drawn from applications. Seeded coordinate changes resist memorizing familiar optimum locations.
entries.caveat: A curated suite; coordinate changes alter difficulty as well as optimum locations.
entries.heritage: Derivative-free optimization, benchmarking and algorithm selection.

entries.title: Covariance-Method Claims Are Ensemble-Relative: Named Measures and an Audit Program
entries.why: Change the matrix ensemble and the verdict can flip. Turns an old warning into a reproducible audit, making covariance comparisons harder to overgeneralize.
entries.caveat: Leaving a method’s stated regime does not refute its theorem.

entries.title: Two Sides of Schur Damping: High-Dimensional Pseudo-Likelihoods and Portfolio Allocation
entries.why: Weather models and portfolios share a damping operation. The attraction is transferring estimation ideas between communities that rarely compare notes.
entries.caveat: Optimal shrinkage is relative to a stated target, loss and model.
entries.heritage: Conditional Gaussians, Vecchia likelihoods and classical shrinkage.

entries.title: Marginally Useful: An Information-Gap Identity in Conformal Prediction
entries.why: Puts an exact log-score price on residual information left unused. A pointed diagnosis of pooling, with more interpretive force than new information theory.
entries.caveat: A fixed residual class, not an unavoidable tax on conformal prediction.

entries.title: The Width of the Conformal Fan: Dependence and the Variance of Realized Coverage
entries.why: Coverage has a spread as well as a mean. Exact cases and counterexamples show how dependence changes the fan across calibration sets.
entries.caveat: Independent marginal test draw; the broad positive-dependence claim remains conjectural.
entries.heritage: Order statistics, Beta laws and dependence theory.
